suggested_experiment_name: White Dwarf Mass-Radius Relation Constraints on Light QCD Axions
notes: Paper constrains exceptionally light QCD axions via white dwarf mass-radius relation. Primary results are exclusion bounds on two parameters: (1) the tuning parameter ϵ in the range 2×10^-20 < ϵ < 2×10^-7 (95% CL, Eq. 15), and (2) the axion decay constant f in the range 5.5×10^9 < f/GeV < 1.1×10^16 (95% CL, Eq. 17). The coupling to nucleons is non-derivative and isospin-symmetric (Eq. 3), with σ_N ≈ 50 MeV. The mechanism involves destabilization of the axion from its in-vacuum minimum at finite baryon density, reducing nucleon mass and altering WD structure. Data extracted from Eqs. (15) and (17) in main text and Appendix B. The bounds are mass-independent in the sense that they constrain parameter space regions rather than specific (m_a, g) pairs. Encoded as horizontal lines spanning stated validity ranges per instructions. Coupling type classified as AxionNeutron because the paper constrains the non-derivative coupling to nucleons (primarily neutrons in dense stellar matter), though the paper does not explicitly separate proton vs. neutron couplings. Extraction confidence reduced to 0.65 because the primary observable is a gap in the M-R relation (a structural feature) rather than a direct coupling measurement, and the parameter space is 2-dimensional (ϵ, f) rather than a standard (mass, coupling) plane. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.65, 61)) | Vision: The paper constrains light QCD axions using white dwarf observations. The primary exclusion plot (FIG. 1) shows constraints on the axion parameter space (m_a vs f_a). However, the hint indicates AxionNeutron coupling (g_an) should be the y-axis. The paper discusses axion-nucleon coupling through the isospin-asymmetric term in Eq. (3), which couples to neutrons. The exclusion region (red area in FIG. 1) is bounded by white dwarf observations. The x-axis shows log10(m_a/eV) ranging from -20 to 0, and the y-axis shows log10(f/GeV) ranging from -20 to -5. The lower boundary of the exclusion region traces the white dwarf constraint. Data points were extracted by tracing the lower edge of the red exclusion region from left to right, sampling more densely at corners and less densely on smooth sections. The conversion from f_a (decay constant) to g_an requires additional physics context not fully specified in the provided pages, so confidence is moderate (0.65).
